t: You're at the site of Daly's Theatre, which stood at 2 Cranbourn Street, just off Leicester Square. It opened on 27 June 1893 and was demolished in 1937. It took its name from Augustin Daly, the American theatre manager and playwright who opened a second Daly's here, after one in New York. Charles Phipps, known for designing more than forty theatres, is credited as architect, alongside Spencer Chadwick. George Edwardes, who brought a new era to musical theatre, owned it, and so later did James White, a financier and property developer.
